label: <DEL> (or q) at step 3-5 in short sequences starting with m/k
explanation: Very sparse reset-gate unit (0.03% of steps). 73% of activation mass is on the <DEL> step and the rest almost entirely on input q during the original phase; it never fires in the copy phase or at t<3, and essentially only at t=3..6 (so short sequences, L=3..5, dominate). Strongly conditioned on the first original token: first_tok m (16x lift, 59% of mass) or k (10x, 32%), with small contributions from r/a. Among those, firing is further favored when the previous input is one of s,g,r,f,y,l,u,3. Top activations are <DEL> in L=4 sequences starting with m (e.g. m m c s <DEL>). The base conjunction (<DEL>/q, t=3..5, first_tok m/k) captures ~87% of mass but with only ~12% precision; adding the prev_tok set raises F1 to ~0.37 at the cost of mass recall. Magnitude is highest for first_tok m at t=4; most <DEL> steps of m/k-initial short sequences do not fire, so the unit reflects a fuzzy hidden-state combination rather than a clean rule.
